制作人. 洛根（Logan）副督察长    转呈人. 加赛德（C. Garside）分区巡官

日本及
亲日机构
的活动

四月期间，在日本宪兵队西区分队的支持下，成立了一支“肃清队”，其特定目的是打击极司菲尔地区（在防线范围内）的游击活动。该队办公室位于极司菲尔路92号，由一名叫川野（KAWANO）的日本人负责。据说雇用了约二十名中国人作为秘密特工。据称，越界筑路区域（O.O.L.）西区的鸦片行号和赌窟在被要求后，已承诺每月向该队提供1,000美元的补贴。

四月，“上海市政府”财政局在越界筑路区域（O.O.L.）西区曹家渡村对面、苏州河北岸的曾提棉纱厂附近设立了一个征收粪便捐的办事处。该项捐款是对每车粪便征收的税款，必须在将粪便卸入河中船只以便运往乡下销售之前缴纳。这项新捐税引起了粪车车主的反对，他们已向越界筑路区域（O.O.L.）西区粪便承包商请求援助。

During the month under review, owners of
factories and shops in the Western District, O.O.L.,
continued their opposition to the proposed collection
of a business tax by the Bureau of Finance of the
"Shanghai City Government." They have secretly
organized a "Zau Ka Doo Factory Owners' Lien Nyi
Association (曹家渡廠商聯誼會 )," also
known as the "Western Shanghai Factory Owners' Lien
Nyi Association," with a preparatory office at 1081
Jessfield Road, O.O.L., for the purpose of furthering
their opposition and evading the attention of the
Bureau authorities.

Similar to that current in the other Japanese
occupied areas, anti-British and anti-National
Government propaganda in the form of posters have
been appearing in the extra-Settlement roads area
of the Western District, O.O.L., since the beginning
of April, 1939.

Lawless
Enterprises
In the middle of April, four new opium hongs
came into existence, thus bringing the total number
of such establishments in the Western District,
O.O.L. up to 42. Of this number, twenty-four
opium hongs are members of the Opium Hong Guild,
No.19 Zung Teh Faung, off Jessfield Road, O.O.L.,

    During April, one named YAMADA ( 山 田 )
was appointed by the Japanese Military Police as
Chief of the Shanghai Amusement Supervision
Department, Lane 470, No.9 Yu Yuen Road, O.O.L. to
replace SASAKI who was suspected of having received
bribes amounting to a considerable sum from various

    During the evening of April 9, a hand-grenade
was found in Sing Kong Li, Connaught Road, O.O.L.
between the back doors of House 23 and 24, the
premises of Zung Foong and Yah Zung Opium Hongs
respectively, and was later removed by members of
the Western District Branch Police Bureau, 92
Jessfield Road, O.O.L.    It is suspected that
the placing of the hand-grenade was the work of
two other opium hongs in the same alleyway as the
result of business jealousy.
    At 5 a.m., April 12, a number of armed male
Chinese called at the distribution office of the
Opium Hong Guild, 41 Kong Foh Li, off Brenan Road,
O.O.L., and demanded admission to the premises.
On their demand being refused, the armed men opened
fire through the door of the house but left before
the arrival of the Japanese Military Police.

In the early morning of April 21, a motor
car carrying some thirty tins of opium (some 4,500
ounces in all), while proceeding from south to north
on Jessfield Road to an opium hong on Brenan Road,
O.C.L. was stopped in front of 946 Jessfield Road,
O.C.L., by a number of gangsters armed with Mauser
pistols. Some of the armed men mounted the car and
ordered the chauffeur to drive the car to an unknown
destination.

Assassination
and shooting
affrays

One case of attempted assassination, one
suspected assassination, and one assassination took
place in the Western District, O.O.L., during the
month under review, details of which are given in
a list attached.

Activities of
terrorist gangs

During the morning of April 14, copies of
a mimeographed handbill in the form of a circular,
purporting to have emanated from the "Chinese Youths
Anti-Japanese and Traitors-Extermination Iron & Blood
Corps (中國青年抗日鋤奸鐵血軍 )" were
distributed by unknown Chinese to the shops in the
Western District, O.O.L.    The circular draws the
attention of the residents to the fact that the Corps
is devoting its time to the extermination of traitors

冲突

File No. S. B. D. 9114/0
Date April 1, 1939.

Subject Report on Situation in Western District, O.O.L.
during the month of March, 1939

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Clausen. J. J.

Activities of
Japanese and
Pro-Japanese
Organs

Two outposts were established during March
by the Japanese Military Police in the extra-Settlement
road area in the Western District. One of them is
known as the "Yu Yuen Road Military Police Sub-Station,"
with offices at House 23, Lane 749 Yu Yuen Road, O.O.L.,
the residence of Mr. Tsang Ding Fan (張定), former
Mayor of Greater Shanghai, which was seized by the
Japanese Gendarmerie during February, 1939; the other
was established inside the compound of the Japan-China
Cotton Mill quarters at Penang & Robison Roads corner.

During March, the Western District Branch of
the Police Bureau of the "Shanghai City Government,"
92 Jessfield Road, O.O.L. increased its strength by
forty constables who were transferred from the Reserve
Unit in Pootung. These men are armed with rifles and
pistols and do patrol duty in the vicinity of the
gambling dens and opium hongs in the Western District,
O.O.L.

During the early part of March, the "Western
District Branch of the Bureau of Finance of the
Shanghai City Government," 92 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.,
issued a notice requiring the shops and factories in
the extra-Settlement roads area in the Western
District to pay a business tax as from March 1, 1939.
The majority of the shop and factory owners in that
district are opposed to the collection of the tax

由特别调查员洛根（Logan）撰写，经 C. Clausen. J. J. 转呈。

日本及
亲日机构
的活动

三月份，日本宪兵队在西区越界筑路区域设立了两个前哨站。其中一个被称为“愚园路宪兵分遣队”，办公地点位于越界筑路区（O.O.L.）愚园路749弄23号，此处原为大上海特别市前市长张定凡（Tsang Ding Fan，音译）先生的寓所，该寓所于1939年2月被日本宪兵队查封；另一个前哨站设立在槟榔路（Penang Road）与罗别森路（Robison Road）转角处的日华纱厂宿舍大院内。

三月份期间，“上海市政府”警察局西区分局（地址：越界筑路区极司菲尔路92号）从浦东后备队调入了四十名巡捕，增强了警力。这些人配备步枪和手枪，在越界筑路区西区的赌窟和鸦片行附近执行巡逻任务。

三月上旬，“上海市政府”财政局西区分局（地址：越界筑路区极司菲尔路92号）发布通告，要求西区越界筑路区域的商店和工厂自1939年3月1日起缴纳营业税。该地区大多数商店和工厂主反对征收此税

Assassinations
and shooting
affrays

In order to cloak their activities, the Opium
Hong Guild assumed the title "Hung Shing Company"
(鸿兴公司) during the month of March.

The office of Mr. KITAOKA, Japanese Advisor
to the "Shanghai City Government" in the Jessfield
Area and Officer-in-charge of the opium monopoly in
the extra-Settlement road area in the Western District
was removed in March from 94 Jessfield Road to 92
Jessfield Road, O.O.L.

Four cases of assassination took place in
the Western District, O.O.L., during the month under
review, details of which are given in a list attached.

On March 16, a bomb exploded in the Lee Wei
Loo Gambling den, next to 1182 Yu Yuen Road, injuring
two female and three male Chinese. On March 18, a
copy of a circular was found pasted on Brenan Branch
Road, O.O.L., denouncing the gambling dens for their
rendering of financial assistance to the Japanese
military and instructing them to close down.

Functioning

and searched the premises on suspicion that the

日本顾问北冈（KITAOKA，音译）先生在极司菲尔区域设有办公室，他是“上海市政府”的顾问，也是越界筑路区西区鸦片专卖的负责人，其三月份将其办公室从极司菲尔路94号迁至越界筑路区（O.O.L.）极司菲尔路92号。

在本审查月份内，越界筑路区（O.O.L.）西区发生了四起暗杀案件，详情见附件清单。

the five constables in one patrolling group are armed
with rifles while the remaining one is armed with a
pistol. Each rifle or pistol is equipped with five
rounds of ammunition instead of one as mentioned in
the previous report.

The strength of the "Bureau" and the various
stations under its control in the Western District,
O.C.L., remains unchanged.

------

Lawless Enterprises

At the end of February, 1939, 25 gambling
dens, 101 Hwo Wei Lottery dens and 34 opium hongs
were operating in the Western District, O.O.L.

Of the 34 opium hongs, 13 are members of the
Opium Hong Guild, No.19 Zung Tuh Faung, Jessfield
Road, O.C.L., while the remainder are non-members.
As the result of an agreement with one KITAOKA,
Japanese Advisor to the "Shanghai City Government"
in Jessfield Area and officer-in-charge the opium
monopoly, members of the Opium Hong Guild have been
promised opium supplies by the Japanese Authorities
through the Guild on condition that the Guild accepts
a supply of opium to the minimum value of $100,000.00

Assassinations and shooting affrays

Two cases of assassinations took place in
the Extra-Settlement Roads Area in the Western
District on February 19 and 22. In the latter
case, a Chinese detective constable of the Municipal
Police was fatally wounded during the exchange of
fire between a party of the Municipal Police and
assessins who were making escape following the
commission of an assassination in a teashop on
Singapore Road, O.O.L. Details are given in a
list attached.

On February 21, about ten male Chinese armed
with pistols attacked the Si Tsu An Gambling Den,
181 West Tsu An Paung off Edinburgh Road, O.O.L.
Apart from firing some ten shots into the air, the
armed gangsters smashed the furniture and windows
of the premises, but no person was injured.

暗杀及枪战案件

2月19日和22日，西区越界筑路区发生了两起暗杀案。在后一起案件中，一名工部局警务处的华籍侦探巡长在工部局警队与刺客交火时受致命伤，当时刺客刚在越界筑路区新加坡路的一家茶馆实施暗杀后正在逃逸。详情见附单。

2月21日，约十名持手枪的中国男子袭击了位于越界筑路区爱丁堡路西侧祖安浜路181号的“四祖安”赌窟。武装暴徒除了向空中开枪约十发外，还砸毁了场所内的家具和窗户，但无人受伤。

Subject Addendum to Report on the Situation in the Western District

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

At the beginning of February, the strength of
the Western District Branch of the Police Bureau of
the "Shanghai City Government," 92 Jessfield Road,
O.C.L. was increased from 64 to 290 constables.
A total of 40 rifles and 20 pistols were issued to
the Branch Bureau by the Japanese authorities.
Each rifle and pistol, however, is equipped with
only one round of ammunition apparently as a
precaution against possible mutiny by the constables.
It has been confidentially learned that the members
of this Police Branch have been instructed by the
"Shanghai City Government" to stiffen their attitude
towards the Settlement Authorities regarding matters
concerning jurisdiction over the extra-Settlement
Roads Area in the Western District. On February 7,
four light machine guns and four heavy machine guns
were supplied to this Branch Bureau by the Japanese
Military Police but no ammunition was supplied.
According to instructions accompanying the machine
guns, ammunition will be supplied when required, from
the Western Section of the Japanese Military Police,
(now known as Kaneya Military Police Detachment), 94
Jessfield Road, situated next to the Bureau. The
Japanese Military, in arming the police with machine
guns, would appear to aim at giving confidence to the
policemen that they will have the support of the
former in case any trouble occurs.

（左侧手写批注：D.S.I. Logan 24/2）
（左下角印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 24.2.39）

2月初，“上海市政府”警察局西区分局（地址：越界筑路区极司菲尔路92号）的警力从64名巡长增加至290名。日本当局向该分局配发了共计40支步枪和20支手枪。然而，每支步枪和手枪仅配备一发子弹，这显然是为了防止巡长可能发生哗变的一种预防措施。据秘密获悉，“上海市政府”已指示该警察分局成员，在涉及西区越界筑路区管辖权的问题上，对租界当局采取强硬态度。2月7日，日本宪兵队向该分局提供了4挺轻机枪和4挺重机枪，但未提供弹药。根据随机枪附带的指示，弹药将在需要时由位于该局隔壁极司菲尔路94号的日本宪兵队西区（现称金谷宪兵分队）供应。日军向警察提供机枪，似乎旨在让警察相信，一旦发生任何麻烦，他们将获得日方的支持。

截至2月17日，越界筑路区西区运营的赌窟和“花会”彩票机构数量分别保持在24家和101家。然而，鸦片烟馆的数量已从18家增加到34家。

附上越界筑路区西区所有鸦片烟馆的新名单。

------

暗杀及枪战案件

2月10日及随后的2月13日，位于越界筑路区极司菲尔路1214号的“土安”花会彩票分所，以及位于极司菲尔路星盛里23号的“裕荣记”花会彩票分所，遭到武装暴徒袭击，屋内家具和窗户被砸毁。无人受伤。

2月10日，武装暴徒在袭击花会彩票分所后，还袭击了“上海市政府警察局”曹家渡分所（地址：极司菲尔路1362号）。据报道有一名警察受伤。2月13日，武装暴徒袭击了位于越界筑路区布伦南路553号的“上海市政府”警察分所，造成家具轻微损坏。未报告有人受伤。

1939年2月14日，法华村发生了一起暗杀案。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
**〔印：SECRET〕**
REPORT

**〔框内文字：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / S. B. REGISTRY / No. Shanghai Division 9146 / Date January 30 - 19 39.〕**
S.1, Special Branch Division
Date ____ January 30 - 19 39.

Subject.... Report on the Situation in the Western District

Made by.... D.S.I. Lozan ....Forwarded by.... C. Crawford D S

Following the withdrawal of the Chinese Forces
after three months' fighting, Shanghai fell to the
Japanese on November 12, 1937. The Japanese Forces,
being chiefly engaged in consolidating the suburbs of
Shanghai immediately after the retreat of the Chinese
Forces, for some time neglected to exercise effective
control over the territory situated east of the Shanghai-
Hangchow Railway Line and south of the Soochow Creek.

About the end of November 1937, the Japanese
Authorities turned their attention to that part of the
Extra-Settlement Roads Area in the Western District which
was formerly under the jurisdiction of the defunct Shanghai
City Government and which lies within the perimeter of the
British Defence Force. Japanese Military Police established
their billets in the Kung Dah Cotton Mill, 138 Jessfield
Road, O.O.L. Sometime later headquarters was located at
442 Jessfield Road but was removed to 94 Jessfield Road
at the beginning of February, 1938.

In conjunction with the Japanese Military Police,
members of the Special Service Section of the Japanese
Military Forces were despatched to the Western district,
ostensibly for the purpose of pacifying the residents.
The "Western Shanghai Pacification Section" (now known
as the Western Shanghai Section of the Japanese Military
Special Service Department) was established at No.94
Jessfield Road.

**〔框内文字：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 特别处登记处 / 编号 上海分区 9146 / 日期 1939年1月30日。〕**
S.1，特别处分处
日期 ____ 1939年1月30日。

主题 ____ 关于西区局势的报告

制作人 ____ 副督察长洛赞（Lozan） ____ 转呈人 ____ C. 克劳福德 副督察长

在中国军队经过三个月的战斗后撤退，上海于1937年11月12日沦陷于日军之手。日军在中国军队撤退后立即主要致力于巩固上海郊区，因此在一段时间内忽视了对位于沪杭铁路线以东、苏州河以南地区的有效控制。

大约在1937年11月底，日本当局将注意力转向西区越界筑路区域中 formerly 由已解散的上海市政府管辖且位于英军防卫部队防线范围内的部分。日本宪兵在界外（O.O.L.）极司菲尔路138号的公大纱厂设立了营房。不久后，总部设在极司菲尔路442号，但在1938年2月初迁至极司菲尔路94号。

与日本宪兵配合，日本军方特务机关成员被派往西区，名义上是为了安抚居民。“上海西区绥靖委员会”（现称为日本军方特务部上海西区分部）成立于极司菲尔路94号。

    In fact, the Japanese Western District Military
Police Headquarters and the Western Shanghai Pacification
Section of the Japanese Military Forces are the principal
organizations dominating the Extra-Settlement Roads Area
of the Western District.
    The first problem to which the Japanese directed
their attention was that of forming a Police force to
assist them in maintaining law and order.  On December 13,
1937, Japanese Military Police convened a meeting of
Chinese shop owners and Japanese residents in the Kung Dah
Cotton Mill, 138 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., during which it
was decided to organize a Police Bureau in the Western
District, with a detective squad selected from the
personnel of the Japanese Military Police garrisoned in
that district, for the purpose of conducting investigations
into the activities of Chinese anti-Japanese elements.
    As the result of this meeting, the Jessfield Police
Station was established at 1091 Jessfield Road during the
latter part of December, 1937 with one Lee Vee-chow
( 李 维 周 ) as the chief, who was recommended to the
post by the Japanese mill owners in the Western District.
This station functioned under the direct supervision of
the Japanese Military Police until February 5, 1938, when
it was taken over by the Western Branch of the Police
Bureau of the "Shanghai Dah Dao City Government", which
was inaugurated in Pootung on December 5, 1937.

    事实上，日本西区宪兵司令部和日本军方上海西区绥靖委员会是主导西区越界筑路区域的主要组织。
    日本人关注的第一个问题是组建一支警察部队以协助他们维持治安。1937年12月13日，日本宪兵在界外（O.O.L.）极司菲尔路138号的公大纱厂召开了中国店主和日本居民会议，会上决定在西区组建一个警察局，并从驻扎在该区的日本宪兵人员中挑选组成一个侦探队，目的是调查中国反日分子的活动。
    作为此次会议的结果，济斯菲尔德路警察局于1937年12月下旬在极司菲尔路1091号成立，由李维周（Lee Vee-chow）担任局长，此人是由西区日本工厂主推荐的。该警局在日本宪兵的直接监管下运作，直到1938年2月5日，由1937年12月5日在浦东成立的“上海大道市政府”警察局西区分局接管。

In cooperation with the members of the Japanese Special

were made afterwards for similar purposes. Between

Police sealed the residences of five Chinese high
officials of the National Government located in the
Extra-Settlement Roads Area of the Western District.

(2) WESTERN SHANGHAI SECTION OF THE JAPANESE MILITARY
SPECIAL SERVICE DEPARTMENT (formerly known as the
WESTERN SHANGHAI PACIFICATION SECTION OF THE
JAPANESE MILITARY FORCES)

    Since the withdrawal of the Chinese troops from
the Shanghai area, the Japanese Special Service
Department has been more openly active than formerly.
Shortly after the fall of this Municipality, the
Japanese special service department formed a branch in
the western district entitled "The Western Shanghai
Pacification Section of the Japanese Military Forces"
with an office situated in No.94 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.
One Mr. SAKURAI was then chief of the section.  It
cooperated closely with the Japanese Military Police
from the very outset in tracing the anti-Japanese
elements and organizations as well as the property of
Chinese officials.  In this connection, large numbers
of Chinese agents recruited from the loafer class were
employed to assist the Japanese in such secret activities.

    At the end of June, 1938, this section was
dissolved because the business situation in the Western
district was alleged to have returned to "normalcy."
To replace the "Pacification Section," the "Western
Shanghai Section of the Japanese Military Special
Service Department" was formed at Lane 37, No.119
Brenan Road, O.O.L., with one TANIKAWA in charge, and
was later removed to 94 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.

(2) 日本军方特务部上海西区分部（前身为“日军上海西区绥靖科”）

    自中国军队撤离上海地区以来，日本特务部的活动较以往更为公开。在本市沦陷后不久，日本特务部在西区设立了一个分支机构，名为“日军上海西区绥靖科”，办公地点位于越界筑路区域极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）94号。当时该科科长为樱井（SAKURAI）先生。从一开始，该科便与日本宪兵队密切合作，追查反日分子和组织以及中国官员的财产。为此，他们雇佣了大量从游民阶层中招募的中国密探，协助日本人进行此类秘密活动。

    1938年6月底，据称由于西区的商业局势已恢复“正常”，该科被解散。为取代“绥靖科”，在越界筑路区域北四川路（Brenan Road）119弄37号成立了“日本军方特务部上海西区分部”，由谷川（TANIKAWA）负责，后迁至越界筑路区域极司菲尔路94号。

(4) OPIUM SMUGGLING PREVENTION CORPS

        The Opium Smuggling Prevention Corps was
inaugurated in January, 1939 under the auspices of
one Mr. KITAOKA, Japanese Advisor to the "Shanghai
City Government" in Jessfield Area. An office is
located at Lane 61, House 21, Kinnear Road. This
Corps is composed of two sections, one dealing with
cases in which Japanese and Korean smugglers are
involved while the other investigates cases in which
only Chinese are concerned. The expenses of this Corps
are defrayed with the monthly fees of $50.00 collected
from each opium hong existing in the Western District,
O.O.L.

        A similar organization entitled the "General
Opium Suppression Bureau for Kiangsu, Chekiang and
Anhwei" is learned to have been formed about the end
of December, 1938, with offices located on 5th floor
of the Broadway Mansions, North Soochow Road, for the
purposes of putting into operation a general opium
monopoly scheme, embracing the provinces of Kiangsu,
Chekiang and Anhwei, to provide revenue to meet urgent
military expenses. However, full details of the
activities of this organization are at present unknown.

    With the inauguration of the "Shanghai Dah Dao
City Government" in Pootung on December 5, 1937, the
following branch offices of the various subordinate organs

under the direct supervision of the Japanese Military
Police.

(2) AN TSING LEAGUE (formerly known as the EAST ASIA
HUANG DAO ASSOCIATION)

Noted for its numerous terrorist activities
committed in the Settlement and French Concession, the
"East Asia Huang Dao Association" was organized in
March, 1938, under the auspices of the Japanese
Authorities, with an office in Room 330, New Asia
Hotel, Tiendong Road. Zang Nyoh-tsing ( 常玉清 ),
a notorious Chinese loafer and criminal, for whose arrest
a warrant has been issued by the Shanghai Special District
Court at the request of the Municipal Police, was the
president of the association. Its principal object was
to assist the Japanese in their secret activities along
the following lines :
(a) undertaking secret investigations on anti-Japanese
organizations (2) keeping general observation on schools,
amusement resorts, hotels, lodging houses, etc., and
(3) terrorising the public by throwing handgrenades, as
a means to combat anti-Nippon@im and Communism in Shanghai.

The creation of a branch in the Western District
was foreshadowed by the appearance of the members of the
association on May 10, 1938, who were engaged in making
investigations along Robison and Kiaochow Roads.
Loh Ping-zien ( 陸炳泉 ), chief of the Special Service
Section of the Association was held responsible by Zang
Nyoh-tsing for recruiting members in the neighbourhood
of Tsai An Pang, Ferry Road. He was further instructed
to organize labour unions in the Western district, O.O.L.,

activities amongst the labourers in the employ of

believed to be a similar organization to the Chinese

Labourers' Welfare Association is closely affiliated
with the "Shanghai Municipality Extra-Settlement Roads

------

对工部局权力的侵蚀

自上海沦陷以来，日本军方当局及其扶植的行政机构多次侵蚀上海工部局的权力。逮捕和搜查行动在租界内故意进行，既未向主管当局申请协助，也未事先通报。数次，所谓“上海大道市政府”（现更名为“上海市政府”）的中国警察在工部局道路上行动，同时税务官员向迄今一直向工部局缴纳市政捐税的居民征收捐税。伪税务局成员强行扣押外人财产的案件也已引起市政警察的注意。

ronins. Within the first two weeks of February,
no less than fourteen gambling dens came into existence.
By the middle of March, 1938, these dens were closed
down by order of the Japanese Military Police, but a
number of them succeeded in obtaining permission from
the Japanese authorities to re-open after payment of

LAWLESS CONDITIONS IN THE WESTERN DISTRICT, O.O.L.

Following the assumption of control by the Japanese
Military Authorities and their sponsored administrative
organs, conditions in the Western District, O.O.L. went
from bad to worse. In consequence of the existence of
many lawless enterprises in the Western district, the place
has become the haunt of every type of undesirable character,
as well as a good shelter for armed robber gangs, who have
committed numerous crimes with impunity. On several occasions,
members of the Municipal Police while on patrol were attacked
by those criminals, and in one case the gangsters committed a
daring highway robbery when foreigners driving in motor cars
on Columbia Road were held up and robbed of money and
jewellery.

Assassination and bombing incidents in the Western
District, O.O.L., have been frequent occurrences, several of
which having taken place in the gambling dens and opium hongs.
Most of these outrages are traceable to gambling and opium
dealing disputes.

朝鲜人经营，同时雇用了一批越界筑路区（西区）的闲散人员作为销售代理。欲从该店购买海洛因的人需先向这些销售代理支付拟购买数量的货款，然后由他们陪同前往该店。不同数量的海洛因被分装在形似香烟盒的不同包装中。

越界筑路区（西区）的无法无天状况

在日本军事当局及其扶植的行政机构接管控制权后，越界筑路区（西区）的局势每况愈下。由于西区存在许多非法企业，该地已成为各类不良分子的聚集地，也是武装抢劫团伙的良好庇护所，这些团伙犯下无数罪行却未受惩罚。市政警察成员在巡逻时曾多次遭到这些罪犯的攻击，其中一起案件中，匪徒在哥伦比亚路上公然拦截驾驶汽车的外国人，抢劫其钱财和珠宝。

越界筑路区（西区）的暗杀和爆炸事件频繁发生，其中有几起发生在赌馆和鸦片行内。大多数这些暴行可追溯至赌博和鸦片交易纠纷。

APPENDIX "A"

Cases of Illegal Functioning in the Western District

1. On January 27, 1938, constables from the "Jessfield Police Station" armed with batons, started functioning on and near Brenan Piece, one being detailed for post duty on Brenan Piece near Robison Road, one on Brenan Piece near Brenan Road, one on Jessfield Road and Connaught Road junction and one on Brenan Road outside the Kincheng Bank, with several Chinese sergeants in plain clothes supervising. They subsequently withdrew from those places after representations were made by the Municipal Police.

2. On June 1, 1938, members of the Japanese Military Police from 94 Jessfield Road, forcibly removed a Chinese chauffeur from the main office of the Ford Hire Service, Edinburgh Road, and returned him to the St. George's Branch Office about one hour later after having interrogated him regarding the movements of certain Japanese officers who had used the car driven by him. According to the chauffeur, two Japanese military officers, accompanied by several Chinese and Japanese civilians, proceeded in his motor car from Hongkew to Lane 152 Edinburgh Road where they forced an elderly Chinese (name, etc., unknown) into the car and carried him off later alighting on North Szechuen Road near Haining Road where they discharged the chauffeur.

3. On July 13, 1938, members from the "Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei Revenue Bureau" (Head office at Kiukiang Road) seized five cases of beer, the property of the Union Brewery (British) in Lane 35-G Brenan Road, O.O.L. The "Bureau" refused to release the seized goods until the Brewery had acknowledged the validity of the "Bureau" to levy tax and had made payment of all the revenue tax due on sales made locally and in the interior.

4. On July 19, a police constable attached to the "Singapore Road Police Sub-Station of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai Municipal Administrative Office" (now known as the "Shanghai City Government"), 476/8 Connaught Road, seized 144 bottles of mineral waters from a male Chinese delivery coolie on Jessfield Road because the bottles did not bear stamps of the tax bureau. of th

5. On July 22, 1938, members of the "Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei Revenue Bureau" forcibly stopped a motor truck belonging to Messrs. Caldbeck, Macgregor & Co., Ltd. (British) on Edinburgh Road near Brenan Road, O.O.L. The truck was ordered to drive to 92 Jessfield Road, where the vehicle and contents were detained. Altogether seventeen crates of mineral water (nine empty) were kept by this "Bureau" because no stamp tax had been paid in respect of the mineral waters. The property was later released after $10 worth of tax stamps had been purchased. A protest to Mr. KITOAKA, Japanese advisor to the "Shanghai Municipal Administrative Office" in Jessfield Area, against members of the "Bureau" operating on Municipal roads brought forth a promise that he would instruct tax inspectors not to operate on S.M.C. roads.

附件“A”

西区非法行事案例

1. 1938年1月27日，“兆丰公园路捕房”的警员手持警棍，开始在白利南块及附近区域行事，其中一人被指派在白利南块靠近罗别根路处站岗，一人在白利南块靠近白利南路处，一人在兆丰公园路与康纳脱路交界处，还有一人在金城银行外的白利南路上，另有几名便衣中国巡长进行监督。随后，在市政警察提出交涉后，他们从这些地方撤离。

2. 1938年6月1日，来自兆丰公园路94号的日本宪兵队成员，强行从爱丁堡路福特租赁服务公司总办事处带走一名中国司机，并在就某些使用该司机驾驶车辆的日本军官的行踪对其进行讯问后，约一小时将其送回圣乔治分行办事处。据该司机称，两名日本军官 accompanied by 几名中日平民，乘坐他的汽车从虹口前往爱丁堡路152弄，在那里强行将一名老年中国人（姓名等不详）塞入车内并带走，随后在北四川路靠近海宁路处下车，解雇了该司机。

3. 1938年7月13日，“江苏浙江安徽税务局”（总局位于九江路）的成员在越界筑路区白利南路35-G弄扣押了联益啤酒厂（英资）的五箱啤酒。该“局”拒绝释放被扣货物，直到啤酒厂承认该“局”征税的有效性，并支付了所有本地及内地销售应缴的税款。

4. 7月19日，隶属于“上海市政办公署警察局新加坡路分驻所”（现称“上海市政府”）康纳脱路476/8号的一名巡警，在兆丰公园路上从一名中国男性送货苦力处扣押了144瓶矿泉水，原因是瓶身上没有税务局的印花税票。of th

5. 1938年7月22日，“江苏浙江安徽税务局”的成员在越界筑路区爱丁堡路靠近白利南路处，强行拦截了一辆属于卡尔贝克·麦格雷戈有限公司（英资）的卡车。该车被命令驶往兆丰公园路92号，车辆及所载物品被扣留。该“局”共扣押了十七箱矿泉水（其中九箱为空箱），原因是矿泉水未缴纳印花税。在购买了价值10美元的印花税票后，财物随后被释放。针对该“局”成员在市政道路上行事的行为，向静安寺地区“上海市政办公署”日本顾问北冈先生（KITOAKA）提出的抗议，换来了一项承诺，即他将指示税务稽查员不在工部局道路上行事。

They were escorted to Pootoo Road Station by members of the U.S. Marine Corps, but were later handed over to the Japanese Authorities on the understanding that they would be duly punished.

They were finally stopped by the Shanghai Municipal Police on Edinburgh Road near Yu Yuen Road and taken to B'Well Station. The two Japanese were later handed over to the Japanese Consular Authorities while the two Chinese were released by the S.M.P.

11. 1938年9月23日，两名日本人和三名自称是“上海市政办公署”官员的中国男子访问了位于越界筑路区新加坡路45号的西方乳品公司，并命令女店主离开该场所，声称该乳品公司是其分居丈夫的财产，但除了向警方报案外，该命令未被理会，此后也未再有人来访。

针对西区前中国政府官员寓所的行动

1. 1938年1月30日，国民政府立法院院长孙科博士位于哥伦比亚路22号的寓所被日本宪兵查封。（现正被亲日组织“大同社”用作其分部办事处）。

2. 1938年2月4日，国民政府前交通部部长王法勤先生位于愚园路31号1136弄的寓所，在所有物品被搬空后，被日本宪兵查封。

3. 1938年2月9日，中央政治委员会主席唐精卫（音译，T'ang Ching-wei）先生位于爱文义路139号的寓所被日本宪兵查封。

4. 2月18日，前上海特别市市长俞鸿钧（O.K. Yui，音译）先生位于布伦路119号37弄的寓所被日本宪兵查封。

5. 1938年7月26日，日本宪兵从前上海市市长吴铁城将军位于海格路464号的寓所（O.O.L.区域），将五卡车家具和古玩运往其北四川路总部。
